overview.text: The Common Wolf Snake is a small, non-venomous snake of South-east Asia and the islands as far as Timor. Its big front teeth, like a wolf's, give it its name.

identification.text: Slender; black, reddish-brown or dark grey with white or yellowish speckles and spots. A squarish snout.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Myanmar, Thailand, Indochina, south-eastern China, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Timor-Leste and the Philippines; also Christmas Island.

behaviour.text: Nervous when handled and quick to bite, but the bite only causes pain and swelling.

recognise.text: Dark body with pale speckles and a squarish snout.
